headline: Growth accelerates, debt climbs to fund acquisition spree
summary_short: APi Group's Q2 2026 revenue rose 13.3% y/y to $2,254M with operating income up 22.4% y/y to $175M and net income up 28.6% y/y to $99M ($0.20 diluted EPS), while long-term debt grew 27.8% y/y to $3,523M funding $816M of year-to-date acquisitions.
summary_long: Revenue grew 13.3% y/y to $2,254M on higher inspection/service/monitoring revenue, project growth, pricing, and acquisitions; Safety Services net revenue +8.8% y/y, Specialty Services +22.9% y/y. Gross margin held near flat at 31.2% (+30bp y/y) as disciplined pricing offset mix. SG&A rose 11.9% y/y on acquisition-related and amortization costs, but SG&A ex-amortization fell to 20.5% of revenue as growth outpaced expense growth. Net income rose 28.6% y/y to $99M ($0.20 diluted EPS). No forward guidance was given in this 10-Q. Cash rose to $851M and long-term debt to $3,523M (+27.8% y/y) after a $500M senior-notes issuance and a Ninth Amendment upsizing the revolver, funding $816M of year-to-date acquisitions including CertaSite and Onyx Fire.

drivers.explanation: MD&A cites solid growth in inspection/service/monitoring revenue, robust project revenue growth, contributions from acquisitions completed in the prior 12 months, and pricing improvements.
Margin was roughly flat at 31.2% (+30bp y/y); MD&A attributes the expansion to disciplined customer/project selection and pricing, partly offset by project and business mix.
MD&A attributes the y/y increase to revenue growth outpacing the 11.9% rise in SG&A; the sequential q/q jump is not separately explained in the release.
Company attributes the increase primarily to strong revenue growth, partially offset by the increase in SG&A expenses.
Not separately explained in the release; follows from higher net income, only partly offset by a larger diluted share count (436.9M vs 427.6M y/y).

Debt rose after the company issued $500M of new 5.750% Senior Notes in May 2026 and upsized/extended its Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loan via the Ninth Amendment, funding acquisition activity including CertaSite and Onyx Fire.

Both segments grew — Safety Services revenue +8.8% y/y, Specialty Services +22.9% y/y — with segment earnings margins expanding in both; the quarter's cash use was dominated by $816M of acquisitions funded by new debt and cash on hand.
